config.title: useImperativeHandle

intro.title: useImperativeHandle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with a custom input component that uses the useImperativeHandle hook to expose a focus method to its parent. You will learn how useImperativeHandle allows child components to customize the instance value exposed to parent components when using refs. The main technologies involved are React functional components, the useRef and useImperativeHandle hooks, and JSX for structuring the UI. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to managing imperative actions in React, helping you understand how to control child component behavior from a parent.
intro.usecase: useImperativeHandle is commonly used in component libraries and complex UI systems where parent components need to directly control child component behavior. For example, in form libraries, parent form components often need to programmatically trigger validation or focus on specific input fields within child components. In dashboard applications with multiple interactive panels, a parent dashboard might need to reset all child chart components to their default state with a single 'reset' button. This hook is also valuable in modal systems where the parent needs to imperatively show/hide modals, or in custom video player components where the parent needs to control playback functions like play, pause, and seek.

objectives: Implement a functional component that uses forwardRef to expose a DOM element
Apply the useImperativeHandle hook to customize the instance value exposed to a parent component
Construct a parent component that creates a ref and passes it to a child component
Manipulate child component methods from a parent component using the exposed imperative handle
Initialize and control a ref to manage focus on an input element via imperative commands
Integrate useImperativeHandle with forwardRef to restrict parent access to specific child functionalities
Render a UI where parent component buttons trigger child component methods through the exposed ref

steps.title: Create a child component with forwardRef

steps.hint: Use forwardRef to wrap your component function. The component should take props and ref as parameters.

// Create your ChildInput component with forwardRef here

steps.title: Define exposed methods in useImperativeHandle
steps.instruction: Inside the useImperativeHandle hook in your ChildInput component, return an object with a method named 'focus' that calls the focus() method on the input element's DOM node.
steps.hint: The useImperativeHandle hook should return an object. The 'focus' method inside that object should call inputRef.current.focus().
steps.expectedOutcome: The useImperativeHandle hook now exposes a 'focus' method that the parent component can call through the ref.
